clue.text: Require backing to secure record increase

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the reversed word wraps around the record
backing tells us the word for 'require' is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to require something is to need it
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone needs support to lock in a bigger record figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the verb, giving DEEN; 'record' is the old extended-play disc, not a best-ever figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen something is to intensify or make it greater, a synonym for increase.

clue.text: Drake's quest at sea, solo bound?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the two words get muddled

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake sails off alone on a voyage of discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' is the anagram signal for SOLO BOUND; the question mark admits the definition is a picture rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake the Elizabethan privateer raided Spanish treasure ships for gold coins of this Spanish kind.

clue.text: One shunning company's brief in Eastern Europe

indicators.note: in places the word for 'brief' inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: a brief is a remit, the scope of a task given to someone

explanation.surface: A loner's job description is to cover Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'), and REMIT sits between E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or recluse lives apart from other people, avoiding society.

clue.text: Pet's anorexia brought out irritation

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters are drawn out and reshaped into a new word

parts.note: the letters of Pet's, the S included, are used

explanation.surface: An owner is annoyed that their animal has stopped eating.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'Pet's' counts as a letter: PETS plus ANOREXIA gives twelve letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperation is intense annoyance, a stronger form of irritation.

clue.text: Stick notice in top right-hand corner?

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a public notice
this entry sits in the top right-hand corner of the grid, so its position is 'here'

explanation.surface: An instruction to pin a notice in a particular spot on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to its own place in the grid: 4 across occupies the top right-hand corner, so that location is HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fastened, a synonym of stick.

clue.text: Chest in the pits gets worse

indicators.note: in places the chest inside the word for the pits

parts.note: dens are lairs or holes, a sense close to pits
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A treasure chest down a mine leads to things going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pits' looks like a mine or a low point, but here it means lairs or holes; 'gets worse' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When a mood or outlook darkens it becomes gloomier, so it deteriorates.

clue.text: Uplift last of the dead

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A funeral phrase about raising up the last of those who died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes E from 'the', then LATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to raise someone's spirits, giving them a lift.

clue.text: Saved artist, complex sort

parts.note: in theology the elect are those chosen for salvation
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter who was rescued turns out to be a complicated character.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electra complex is a term from psychoanalysis, so the name is a sort of complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis names a daughter's fixation on her father after this Greek heroine, a complex parallel to Oedipus.

clue.text: Book has an effect

definitions.meaning: a book of the New Testament
a drug or measure that works on something takes effect on it

explanation.definitionFit: One is the Bible's fifth New Testament book; the other is the verb meaning to work or take effect.

clue.text: End and means to make raised footpath

parts.note: an end is a purpose or aim, as is a cause one works for
a way is a means or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark about ends and means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' here means an aim, as in 'to that end', not a finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a road or path built up above wet ground or water.

clue.text: FBI leaving briefcase out in marked area

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters are rearranged after the agency is taken away

parts.note: the word briefcase supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Federal agents abandon a case found in a cordoned-off zone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take F, B and I out of BRIEFCASE ('leaving'), leaving RECASE; 'out' rearranges those letters. The crease in cricket is the area marked in white lines where the batsman stands.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the creases are white lines painted on the pitch, marking the batsman's safe ground.

clue.text: Much to be thought about?

definitions.meaning: read literally as able to be considered, worth thinking over

explanation.definitionFit: It means sizeable or large, and broken down it describes something capable of being weighed up in the mind.

clue.text: One's working for promotion?

parts.note: reads like an ambitious employee chasing a better job, but means bettering one's own self through effort

explanation.definitionFit: Working to make oneself a better person is promoting one's own development.

clue.text: Prepares in advance, with attention boosting arrangements

indicators.note: the attention word is pushed into the middle of the arrangements, building them up from within

parts.note: forms are arrangements or shapes
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready early, paying close attention to the plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosting' looks like it means help, but it signals one piece placed inside another; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To forearm is to equip or ready someone beforehand, as in forewarned is forearmed.

clue.text: Dress for taking the air when down in South Island

definitions.text: Dress for taking the air when down

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A diver's outfit for breathing, worn in a southern island resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'Dress' means outfit, and 'down' means underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers wear self-contained breathing apparatus and a suit so they can breathe below the surface.

clue.text: Infectious jester leaving top? I'll say!

indicators.note: leaving top means the first letter of the down entry's word for jester drops away

parts.note: a funster is a joker or jester

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be spoken, giving the sound 'isle'

parts.note: I'll is pronounced like isle

explanation.surface: A clown with a nasty bug loses his cap, and someone exclaims about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving top' takes F off FUNSTER; 'say' turns I'll into its sound, spelt ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not sterile carries germs, so it can pass on infection.

clue.text: A sign of unpreparedness for expedition

definitions.meaning: rushing about is a sign that someone has not got ready in time
expedition in its old sense of promptness or speed

explanation.definitionFit: Hurrying shows a lack of preparation, and expedition means speed of action.

clue.text: Lodge with associate

definitions.meaning: to lodge somewhere is to live or stay there
to associate with people is to spend time with them

explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to reside somewhere informally, or to keep company with friends.

clue.text: One exposing former philosopher king

parts.note: ex means former
David Hume was a Scottish philosopher
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch who was once a thinker reveals secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a philosopher king, but it is three pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who digs up a buried body brings it out into the open.

clue.text: Insisted upon exercise, in good shape

indicators.note: exercise puts the letters through their paces, moving them into a new order

explanation.surface: A trainer demanded workouts to keep fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon exercise' rearranges INSISTED; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat, orderly state is being in good shape.

clue.text: Catching fish after boy's given up

indicators.note: after puts the fish behind the reversed name
given up in a down clue means the boy's name is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Ian is a boy's name; the 's stands for 'is'
the ling is a sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler lands a fish once the lad has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'given up' reads the name from bottom to top, giving NAI; 'Catching' is meant in the sense of collaring a culprit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing a criminal is catching them, in the informal sense.

clue.text: One may lose this with huge binliners so untidy

indicators.note: untidy signals the letters are in a mess and need sorting

explanation.surface: Leaving enormous rubbish bags in a mess costs you your friendly relations with the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges HUGE BINLINERS SO; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendliness towards the people living next door is what one forfeits by being a nuisance.

clue.text: Clothe in tribute?

parts.note: a due is a payment owed, like a tribute

explanation.surface: A question about dressing someone in a fitting homage.
explanation.walkthrough: INDUE is an old variant of ENDUE, to clothe or invest.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue, also spelt indue, is to put on or invest someone with garments.

clue.text: Bore son in Cambodia

parts.note: K is the international vehicle registration code for Cambodia

explanation.surface: A tedious son living in Cambodia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' means drill, not a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a well or shaft is to drill it into the ground.

clue.text: Old drug's taken -made ill with swelling

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug; the 's is a link meaning 'has'

indicators.note: ill suggests the word is in poor condition and must be reshaped

explanation.surface: Taking an old drug left someone ill and puffed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's dash is surface punctuation; 'ill' scrambles the four letters of 'made', giving DEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedema is a medical condition in which fluid builds up in tissue and makes it puffy.

clue.text: Draw bow back, not the last playing violin with Nirvana

indicators.note: back with draw means the shortened word is pulled back, read from end to start
not the last removes the final letter of the word for the archer's weapon

parts.note: the word bow taken as written

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with

explanation.surface: A musician draws the bow back while playing the violin, lost in bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the last' trims BOW to BO and 'Draw ... back' turns it into OB; 'playing' rearranges VIOLIN into LIVION.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the extinction of the self, a state of nothingness or forgetting.

clue.text: Man stopping Conservative speculation

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the man sits inside the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man blocks a Tory, leading to guesswork.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or idea not yet proved, which is what speculation offers.

clue.text: Measure all the sides

definitions.meaning: an old unit of distance of about three miles
all the teams competing together in one competition

explanation.definitionFit: It is both an old unit of length of roughly three miles and a sports competition made up of every team.
